{{Short description|American-Argentinian natural historian (1935–2015)}}
'''Rae Natalie Prosser de Goodall''' (née '''Rae Natalie Prosser''') April 13, 1935, near [[Lexington, Ohio]], United States – May 25, 2015, [[Estancia Harberton]], [[Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina]],<ref name="sur54">{{cite web|url=http://www.sur54.com/falleci-ayer-en-la-estancia-harberton-la-destacada-biloga-natalie-goodall|website=sur54.com|title=Falleció ayer en la estancia Harberton la destacada bióloga Natalie Goodall|access-date=2018-01-15|archive-date=2018-01-16|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180116081133/http://www.sur54.com/falleci-ayer-en-la-estancia-harberton-la-destacada-biloga-natalie-goodall|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="tiempofueguino">{{cite web|url=http://www.tiempofueguino.com/21467-fallecio-natalie-prosser-de-goodal-pionera-de-la-investigacion-en-la-provincia.html|website=tiempofueguino.com|title=Falleció Natalie Prosser de Goodal, pionera de la investigación en la provincia|date=26 May 2015|access-date=2018-01-15|archive-date=2015-05-27|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150527205506/http://www.tiempofueguino.com/21467-fallecio-natalie-prosser-de-goodal-pionera-de-la-investigacion-en-la-provincia.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>) also known as '''Natalie Goodall''', was a [[botanist]], [[cetologist]], [[illustrator]], [[natural historian]] and [[local historian]] based in [[Tierra del Fuego Province, Argentina]] and known for studying the region's [[flora]] and [[fauna]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Pisani |first=Silvia |title=La mujer que estudia las ballenas en el Sur|url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/nota.asp?nota_id=108889|publisher=La Nación|access-date=2010-10-30|date=1998-08-31}}</ref>

==Education==
Rae Natalie Prosser de Goodall was born Rae Natalie Prosser on a farm near Lexington, Ohio.<ref name="LN">{{cite web|last=Bocchicchio|first=Silvio |title=La primera estancia fueguina se convirtió en museo de fósiles|url=http://www.lanacion.com.ar/nota.asp?nota_id=687105|publisher=La Nación|access-date=2010-10-30|date=2005-03-13}}</ref> She graduated from Lexington High School in 1953.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Caudill |first=Mark |title=Lexington native lived for nature |url=https://www.mansfieldnewsjournal.com/story/news/local/2015/06/01/botany-marine-biology-goodall/28324059/ |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=Mansfield News Journal |language=en-US}}</ref> She was awarded an art scholarship to [[Kent State University]], where she became a member of the [[Gamma Phi Beta]] sorority.{{Citation needed|date=November 2024}} Prosser graduated with [[bachelor's degree]]s<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Schiavini |first=Adrián |date=2015-08-24 |title=Rae Natalie Prosser de Goodall 1935-2015 |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q130766544 |journal=The Latin American Journal of Aquatic Mammals |volume=10 |issue=1 |pages=68–69 |doi=10.5597/LAJAM00198|doi-access=free }}</ref> in [[education]], [[biology]], and [[art]], as well as a [[master's degree]] in biology.{{Citation needed|date=November 2024}} She was awarded an honorary doctorate from Kent State University in 1997.<ref name=":1" /> 

== Career ==
Despite a busy and challenging life managing [[Estancia Harberton]] and family on the [[Beagle Channel]] in the 1960s, Goodall found the time and energy to study and draw the natural history, flora and fauna of the surrounding area, and eventually of [[Tierra del Fuego]] as a whole.<ref name=":1" /> She began collecting and drawing plants, with her herbarium becoming the basis for understanding the flora of the island, and together with her drawings, an important foundation for a later book to which she contributed, ''Flora of Tierra del Fuego''.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Cabrera |first=Review By: A. L. |date=1984-01-01 |title=Flora of Tierra del Fuego by David M. Moore |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q104175093 |journal=Darwiniana |language=Spanish |volume=25 |issue=1/4 |pages=385–386}}</ref> 

A self-described "beachcomber", Goodall also started collecting dolphin and whale specimens during this time, especially skulls, from local [[Cetacea|cetacean]] strandings.<ref name=":1" /> Over the course of her life, she collected nearly 3000 mammal specimens and initially curated these together with her 2500 bird skeletons (and hundreds of plant specimens<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Rae Natalie Prosser de Goodall |url=https://bionomia.net/Q6096868 |access-date=2024-11-03 |website=bionomia.net |language=en}}</ref>) at her home in Harberton.<ref name=":1" /> Goodall also kept records of observations of sightings of living dolphins and whales that she made herself, or that others in the area provided to her.<ref name=":1" /> In this way, she became a world expert in southern South American [[cetology]] and botany.<ref name=":1" /> 

Goodall collected plants with several other notable botanists including [[Lincoln Constance]], [[Alicia Lourteig]], [[Theodore Robert Dudley]], [[David Moore (botanist born 1933)|David Moore]], and others.<ref name=":2" /> She also collaborated with dozens of botanical and cetacean researchers from around the world. 

In 2001, Goodall donated and curated items from her personal collection to create the Acatushun Museum of Austral Birds and Mammals (Museo Acatushun) on the grounds of Estancia Harberton.<ref>{{cite web|title=Museo Acatushun|url=http://www.acatushun.com|publisher=Fundación R. Natalie P. Goodall|access-date=2010-10-29|date=2001}}</ref> Many of her specimens are also housed at numerous international herbaria and natural history institutions,<ref name=":2" /> and some of these are the most important specimens in the world, as they represent collections of several little-known and sparsely-collected species of dolphins and whales including ''[[Cephalorhynchus commersonii]], [[Lagenorhynchus australis]], [[Lagenorhynchus cruciger|L. cruciger]], and [[Mesoplodon hectori]]''.<ref name=":1" /> 

She received research funding from the [[National Geographic Society]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Graantees. Natalie Goodall Biologist|url=http://www.nationalgeographic.com/outthere/grantees.html#goodall|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20011126100013/http://www.nationalgeographic.com/outthere/grantees.html#goodall|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 26, 2001|publisher=National Geographic|access-date=2010-10-30}}</ref> and collaborated with other national and international organizations devoted to nature research, including AMMA ([[Association of Southern Marine Mammals]]),<ref>{{cite web|title=El museo comenzó el monitoreo de la costa|url=http://www.eldiariodelfindelmundo.com/noticias/leer/24595|publisher=El Diario del Fin del Mundo|access-date=2010-10-30|date=2009-09-10}}</ref> the [[Orca del Fin del Mundo]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Colaboradores|url=http://www.orcadelfindelmundo.org/colaboradores.htm|publisher=Orca del Fin del Mundo|access-date=2010-10-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090725153445/http://www.orcadelfindelmundo.org/colaboradores.htm|archive-date=2009-07-25}}</ref> project and CEQUA (Center for Quaternary Studies).<ref>{{cite web|title=Estudio revela reducción de la población de toninas que habita en el extremo austral de Chile|url=http://www.latercera.com/contenido/739_280099_9.shtml|publisher=La Tercera.com|access-date=2010-10-30|location=Chile|date=July 29, 2010|archive-date=2015-05-30|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150530062614/http://www.latercera.com/contenido/739_280099_9.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref>  She founded and chaired the [[RNP Foundation]] ([[Rae Natalie Prosser Foundation]]) for biological research in Southern [[South America]], which endows internships and scholarships for students and professionals in the [[natural sciences]].

== Notable works ==
In 1970, Goodall published a bilingual English-Spanish book, ''Tierra del Fuego'', containing studies of the local flora and fauna, as well as historical information about the settlement of the area. She both wrote and illustrated the book, and published several editions of it at the publishing company she founded, [[Ediciones Shanamaiim]].<ref name=":1" /> This book continues to be used both as a tourist guide and a reference manual and is considered an ''[[ad honorem]]'' historical work.  

Goodall was also one of the main contributors and illustrators of [[David Moore (botanist born 1933)|David Moore]]'s 1983 book, ''Flora of Tierra del Fuego.''<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Cantino |first=Philip |date=1984-07-01 |title=Flora of Tierra del Fuego. |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q95460199 |journal=Systematic Botany |language=English |volume=9 |issue=3 |pages=372 |doi=10.2307/2418617|jstor=2418617 |bibcode=1984SysBo...9..372C |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite book |last1=Goodall |first1=Rae Natalie Prosser de |url=https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q130767653 |title=Flora of Tierra del Fuego |last2=Moore |first2=David M. |date=1983-01-01 |publisher=Missouri Botanical Garden |isbn=978-0-904614-05-3 |language=English}}</ref><ref name=":3" /> According to Moore, Goodall should have been co-author on the book, but it was her choice not to be''.''<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":5" /> Her line drawings are described as being an "attractive and informative" part of the book, and her herbarium specimens provided key information about each species.<ref name=":4" />

Some of Goodall's drawings of the plants and wildlife of Tierra del Fuego are in the collection of the [[Hunt Botanical Library]], which is part of the [[Hunt Institute for Botanical Documentation]] at [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in [[Pittsburgh]], [[Pennsylvania]]. She was also featured as a botanical artist in the book ''Botanical Art and Illustration (1972–1973)'', a publication of the Hunt library.<ref>{{cite web |title=List of the artists in Hunt Institute's art collection. |url=http://huntbot.andrew.cmu.edu/HIBD-Beta/HIBD-PDF/HIBD-ArtCat-Artists.pdf |access-date=2010-10-29 |publisher=Hunt Institute for Botanical Documentation Carnegie Mellon University}}</ref> 

==Publications==
Throughout her life, Goodall published over 200 scientific publications, including peer-reviewed papers, book chapters, and scientific conference abstracts.<ref name=":1" /> She also presented her research at international scientific conferences.<ref name=":1" /> Additional notable publications include:

* "Interspecific variation of ontogeny and skull shape among porpoises ([[Phocoenidae]])", in ''[[Journal of Morphology]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=P. Goodall |first1=R. Natalie |last2=Anders Galatius; Annalisa Berta; Marie Schou Frandsen |year=2011 |title=Interspecific variation of ontogeny and skull shape among porpoises (Phocoenidae) |journal=Journal of Morphology |language=English |volume=272 |issue=2 |pages=136–48 |doi=10.1002/jmor.10900 |pmid=20967830 |s2cid=21429242}}</ref>
* "On the identity of ''[[Lagenorhynchus australis|Tursio Chiloensis Philippi]]'' 1900", in ''[[Marine Mammal Science]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last=P. Goodall |first=R. Natalie |date=2006-08-26 |title=On the identity of ''Tursio Chiloensis'' Philippi 1900 |journal=Marine Mammal Science |language=English |volume=2 |issue=3 |pages=230–232 |doi=10.1111/j.1748-7692.1986.tb00044.x}}</ref><ref name="marinespecies">{{cite web |title=WoRMS - World Register of Marine Species - Tursio chiloensis Philippi, 1900 |url=http://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=384177&from=rss |access-date=2018-01-15 |website=marinespecies.org}}</ref>
* "Serrated Flippers and Directional Asymmetry in the Appendicular Skeleton of the [[Commerson's Dolphin]]", in ''[[The Anatomical Record]]''.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=P. Goodall |first1=R. Natalie |last2=Encarna Gómez-Campos; Alex Aguilar |date=2010-11-01 |title=Serrated Flippers and Directional Asymmetry in the Appendicular Skeleton of the Commerson's Dolphin (''Cephalorhynchus commersonii'') |journal=Anatomical Record |language=English |volume=293 |issue=11 |pages=1816–1824 |doi=10.1002/ar.21227 |pmid=20830764 |s2cid=205409762 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Personal life and family ==
She worked as a teacher for [[Mobil]] in [[Venezuela]] after graduating, during which time she traveled extensively in Venezuela, [[Colombia]], and the [[List of Caribbean islands|Caribbean islands]], studying the local plants and wildlife.{{Citation needed|date=November 2024}} On a trip to western [[South America]] with a fellow teacher, Prosser visited the [[Tierra del Fuego]] area, having been inspired by [[Lucas Bridges]]' book ''Uttermost Part of the Earth''.<ref name=":1" /> While on this trip she met her future husband Thomas Goodall, a great-nephew of the book's author and manager of the [[Estancia Harberton]] (Harberton Ranch) featured in the book.<ref name=":1" /> The two were married in the United States in 1963.{{Citation needed|date=November 2024}} 

Goodall and her husband continued to maintain Estancia Harberton for the remainder of her life, raising two daughters, Anne and Abby,<ref name=":0" /> on the ranch and in the nearby city of [[Ushuaia]]. Her husband, children, and six grandchildren<ref name=":0" /> are the fourth, fifth and sixth-generation descendants, respectively, of [[Thomas Bridges (Anglican missionary)|Thomas Bridges]], the builder of Estancia Harberton and an [[Anglican]] [[missionary]] credited with spreading Christianity in the Tierra del Fuego region.

== Death ==
Goodall died of natural causes on May 25, 2015 at home at Estancia Harberton.<ref name=":0" /> Goodall's family has continued to manage Estancia Harberton following her 2015 death.
